'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Israeli–Palestinian conflict]]
**[[2023 Eli shooting]]
***[[Hamas]] kill four [[Israelis]] and injure four others in a [[mass shooting]] at a restaurant and a [[Filling station|petrol station]] near the [[Israeli settlement]] of [[Eli (Israeli settlement)|Eli]] in the occupied [[West Bank]]. The two gunmen are killed by a civilian and a [[Israeli Ground Forces|soldier]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-65963017 (BBC News)]
*Spillover of the [[Somali Civil War (2009–present)|Somali Civil War]]
**Seven people are killed and seven more injured when a police car and a public service vehicle are targeted by two [[improvised explosive device|roadside bombings]] at two different locations in [[Mandera County]], [[Kenya]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/four-killed-north-east-kenya-after-vehicle-runs-over-explosive-2023-06-21/ (Reuters)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[China–Pakistan relations]]
**The [[China National Nuclear Corporation]] and the [[Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission]] sign a [[United States dollar|US$]]4.8 billion deal to construct the fifth unit at the [[Chashma Nuclear Power Plant]], [[Pakistan]]'s [[Nuclear power in Pakistan|seventh]] [[nuclear power plant]], in [[Punjab, Pakistan|Punjab]]. [https://edition.cnn.com/2023/06/20/asia/pakistan-china-nuclear-power-plant-deal-intl-hnk/index.html (Reuters via CNN)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[Whaling in Iceland]]
**[[Ministry of Fisheries and Agriculture (Iceland)|Fisheries and Agriculture Minister]] [[Svandís Svavarsdóttir]] announces that all [[whaling]] operations will be suspended in [[Iceland|the country]] until 31 August at the earliest, citing welfare concerns after a video emerged of a hunted whale dying in agony over a five-hour period. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2023/6/20/iceland-suspends-whale-hunt-on-animal-rights-concerns (Al Jazeera)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[War crimes in Afghanistan]]
**[[Tasmania]]n [[Australian Senate|Senator]] [[Jacqui Lambie]] announces that she has referred several members of the [[Australian Defence Force]] to the [[International Criminal Court]] for alleged [[war crime]]s during the [[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)|war]] in [[Afghanistan]]. [https://www.canberratimes.com.au/story/8240621/adf-leadership-referred-to-international-criminal-court/ (''Canberra Times'')]
*[[Támara prison riot]]
**At least 41 inmates are killed and seven others are injured during a [[prison riot|riot]] at a [[women's prison]] in Támara, near [[Tegucigalpa]], [[Honduras]]. [https://apnews.com/article/honduras-womens-prison-riot-211c6031a29338f7a3da7c1175adfa4e (AP)]
*French police raid the [[Saint-Denis, Seine-Saint-Denis|Saint-Denis]] offices of the [[2024 Summer Olympics|2024 Parisian Summer Olympics]] organization committee and the [[headquarters]] of contracted construction company Solideo, over allegations of corruption. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-65961949 (BBC News)]
*[[Hunter Biden]], son of [[United States President]] [[Joe Biden]], is provided a plea deal for misdemeanor offenses relating to failing to pay federal taxes. A further offense of owning a firearm while lying about being an illegal drug user will be dismissed, following a two-year [[probation]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/live/2023/jun/20/hunter-biden-will-plead-guilty-to-three-federal-charges-court-filing-shows-live-updates (''The Guardian'')]
*Influencer [[Andrew Tate]] is [[criminal charge|charged]] by [[Directorate for Investigating Organized Crime and Terrorism|Romanian authorities]] with [[rape]], [[human trafficking]], and forming an [[organized crime]] group as part of [[Andrew Tate#2022–present Romanian investigation|an ongoing investigation]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-65959097 (BBC News)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2023 Finnish parliamentary election]]
**[[Petteri Orpo]] is officially appointed as the [[Prime Minister of Finland|47th prime minister of Finland]] and forms [[Orpo Cabinet|his cabinet]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/finlands-parliament-backs-petteri-orpo-pm-replacing-sanna-marin-2023-06-20/ (Reuters)]
*[[LGBT rights in Estonia]]
**Estonia passes a bill legalising [[same-sex marriage]] and [[same-sex adoption]] by 2024, becoming the first [[Baltic states|Baltic]] and [[post-Soviet states|post-Soviet]] state to do so. [https://www.cnn.com/2023/06/20/europe/estonia-same-sex-marriage-legal-intl/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Education in South Korea]]
**The [[Ministry of Education (South Korea)|Ministry of Education]] announces plans to reform the [[College Scholastic Ability Test]] by removing questions unrelated to the curriculum taught in [[state school]]s. Education Minister [[Lee Ju-ho]] says that the reform aims to minimize students' dependence on [[hagwon]]s and address the negative consequences of high-pressure education on students, citing the correlation with [[Suicide in South Korea|South Korea's high suicide rates]]. [https://news.abs-cbn.com/overseas/06/20/23/south-korea-cuts-killer-questions-from-college-entrance-exam (AFP via ABS-CBN News)]
